svg.title: Here is the summation principle needed for countably many local comparisons. Suppose the i-th pair of insertions each has a common summable bound fi ≥0, and its difference has a remainder bound tending to zero with the history index. The coarse bound on that difference is 2fi. Given r > 0, choose a finite set E with P i/∈E 2fi ≤r/2. On the finitely many indices in E, eventually choose the common bound v = r/[2(|E|+1)]. Use v on E and 2fi outside. This is a valid per-index bound and its total is at most r. The paid merge bound therefore gives an eventual remainder bound r for the full merged difference. Absolute convergence and the same label enumeration identify this merged difference with the difference of the two merged insertions. The finite core sums converge by the same finite-set/tail split. Thus countably many local comparisons assemble into the full comparison.
